apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: benchmark-job-id
  labels:
    app: benchmark-ai
    action-id: ACTION_ID
    client-id: CLIENT_ID
    created-by: executor
    custom_label: my-value
    other_label: other-value
    parent-action-id: parentactionid
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: benchmark-ai
        action-id: ACTION_ID
        client-id: CLIENT_ID
        created-by: executor
        custom_label: my-value
        other_label: other-value
        parent-action-id: parentactionid
      annotations:
        iam.amazonaws.com/role: benchmark-host
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: benchmark
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - labelSelector:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: app
                operator: In
                values:
                - benchmark-ai
            topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      initContainers: []
      containers:
      - name: benchmark
        image: edisongustavo/bai-benchmarks-hello-world:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 0
        command:
        - python3
        - hello-world.py
        securityContext:
          privileged: false
        env:
        - name: BENCHMARK_AI
          value: fifo
        - name: BENCHMARK_AI_FIFO_FILEPATH
          value: /tmp/benchmark-ai/fifo
        - name: BENCHMARK_AI_FIFO_MAX_WAIT_TIME
          value: '60'
        - name: FIST_VAL
          value: VAR
        - name: SECOND_VAL
          value: VAR
        - name: FOO
          value: bar
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tmp/benchmark-ai
          name: benchmark-ai
        - name: dshm
          mountPath: /dev/shm
      - name: metrics-pusher
        image: benchmarkai/metrics-pusher:ffed580
        env:
        - name: BENCHMARK_AI_FIFO_FILEPATH
          value: /tmp/benchmark-ai/fifo
        - name: BACKEND
          value: kafka
        - name: BACKEND_ARG_ACTION_ID
          value: ACTION_ID
        - name: BACKEND_ARG_CLIENT_ID
          value: CLIENT_ID
        - name: BACKEND_ARG_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: outputs-infrastructure
              key: msk_bootstrap_brokers
        - name: BACKEND_ARG_KEY
          value: CLIENT_ID
        - name: BACKEND_ARG_TOPIC
          value: BAI_METRICS
        - name: POD_NAME
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.name
        - name: POD_NAMESPACE
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.namespace
        - name: CUSTOM_LABEL_CUSTOM_LABEL
          value: my-value
        - name: CUSTOM_LABEL_OTHER_LABEL
          value: other-value
        - name: CUSTOM_LABEL_PARENT-ACTION-ID
          value: parentactionid
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tmp/benchmark-ai
          name: benchmark-ai
      - name: metrics-extractor
        image: benchmarkai/metrics-extractor:b0b9185
        env:
        - name: ANUBIS_POD_NAME
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.name
        - name: ANUBIS_POD_NAMESPACE
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.namespace
        - name: ANUBIS_METRICS
          value: '[{"name": "accuracy", "units": "%", "pattern": "YWNjdXJhY3k9KFstK10/XGQqXC5cZCt8XGQrKQ=="},
            {"name": "throughput", "units": "images/sec", "pattern": "dGhyb3VnaHB1dD0oWy0rXT9cZCpcLlxkK3xcZCsp"}]'
        - name: BENCHMARK_AI
          value: fifo
        - name: BENCHMARK_AI_FIFO_FILEPATH
          value: /tmp/benchmark-ai/fifo
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tmp/benchmark-ai
          name: benchmark-ai
      nodeSelector:
        beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type: t2.small
        node.type: bai-worker
        failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone: us-east-1a
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      volumes:
      - name: benchmark-ai
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: dshm
        emptyDir:
          medium: Memory
  backoffLimit: 4
instruction: We need to deploy a Kubernetes Job named `benchmark-job-id` that runs a benchmarking task. The job should use the `edisongustavo/bai-benchmarks-hello-world:latest` Docker image for the main benchmark container and the `benchmarkai/metrics-pusher:ffed580` and `benchmarkai/metrics-extractor:b0b9185` images for the metrics pusher and extractor containers, respectively. The benchmark container should be configured to run a Python script `hello-world.py` with specific environment variables and resource limits (0 GPUs). The job must ensure pod anti-affinity based on the `app` label to avoid scheduling pods on the same node. Additionally, the job should use a service account named `benchmark` and have specific node selectors for instance type (`t2.small`), node type (`bai-worker`), and availability zone (`us-east-1a`). The job should restart up to 4 times on failure and utilize an empty directory volume named `benchmark-ai` and a memory-based volume named `dshm`. Please include annotations for IAM role assignment and ensure the job is labeled appropriately for tracking and identification purposes.

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: strimzi-cluster-operator
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      name: strimzi-cluster-operator
      strimzi.io/kind: cluster-operator
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        name: strimzi-cluster-operator
        strimzi.io/kind: cluster-operator
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: strimzi-cluster-operator
      containers:
        - name: strimzi-cluster-operator
          image: strimzi/cluster-operator:latest
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          env:
            - name: STRIMZI_NAMESPACE
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.namespace
            - name: STRIMZI_FULL_RECONCILIATION_INTERVAL_MS
              value: "120000"
            - name: STRIMZI_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS
              value: "300000"
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_ZOOKEEPER_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/zookeeper:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/kafka:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_CONNECT_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/kafka-connect:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_CONNECT_S2I_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/kafka-connect-s2i:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_TOPIC_OPERATOR_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/topic-operator:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_INIT_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/kafka-init:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_TLS_SIDECAR_ZOOKEEPER_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/zookeeper-stunnel:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_TLS_SIDECAR_KAFKA_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/kafka-stunnel:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_TLS_SIDECAR_TOPIC_OPERATOR_IMAGE
              value: strimzi/topic-operator-stunnel:0.5.0
            - name: STRIMZI_LOG_LEVEL
              value: INFO
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthy
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 30
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 30
          resources:
            limits:
              memory: 256Mi
              cpu: 1000m
            requests:
              memory: 256Mi
              cpu: 200m
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
instruction: We need to deploy the Strimzi Cluster Operator as a Kubernetes Deployment. The deployment should have exactly one replica and use the `strimzi/cluster-operator:latest` image with the `IfNotPresent` pull policy. The container should run with the `strimzi-cluster-operator` service account and include specific environment variables for namespace, reconciliation interval, operation timeout, and default images for various components (Zookeeper, Kafka, Kafka Connect, etc.). Additionally, the container should have liveness and readiness probes configured to check `/healthy` and `/ready` endpoints on port 8080 with initial delays of 10 seconds and periodic checks every 30 seconds. Resource limits and requests should be set to 256Mi of memory and 1000m/200m of CPU, respectively. The deployment strategy should be set to `Recreate`.

apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1

metadata:
  name: strimzi-cluster-operator-global
  labels:
    name: strimzi-cluster-operator-global
    app.kubernetes.io/component: messaging
    avaloq.com/app: strimzi-operator-definitions
rules:
- apiGroups:
  - "rbac.authorization.k8s.io"
  resources:
  # The cluster operator needs to create and manage cluster role bindings in the case of an install where a user
  # has specified they want their cluster role bindings generated
  - clusterrolebindings
  verbs:
  - get
  - create
  - delete
  - patch
  - update
  - watch
- apiGroups:
  - storage.k8s.io
  resources:
  # The cluster operator requires "get" permissions to view storage class details
  # This is because only a persistent volume of a supported storage class type can be resized
  - storageclasses
  verbs:
  - get
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  # The cluster operator requires "list" permissions to view all nodes in a cluster
  # The listing is used to determine the node addresses when NodePort access is configured
  # These addresses are then exposed in the custom resource states
  - nodes
  verbs:
  - list
instruction:
We need to create a ClusterRole named `strimzi-cluster-operator-global` that grants the necessary permissions to the Strimzi Cluster Operator for managing cluster role bindings and accessing storage class details and node listings. Specifically, the ClusterRole should allow the following actions:

1. On the `clusterrolebindings` resource under the `rbac.authorization.k8s.io` API group, the ClusterRole should permit `get`, `create`, `delete`, `patch`, `update`, and `watch` operations.
2. On the `storageclasses` resource under the `storage.k8s.io` API group, the ClusterRole should permit `get` operations.
3. On the `nodes` resource under the default API group (`""`), the ClusterRole should permit `list` operations.

Additionally, the ClusterRole should be labeled with `name: strimzi-cluster-operator-global`, `app.kubernetes.io/component: messaging`, and `avaloq.com/app: strimzi-operator-definitions`.

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: delete-topics
  namespace: kafka
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      name: delete-topics
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: kafka
        image: solsson/kafka:2.1.1@sha256:8bc8242c649c395ab79d76cc83b1052e63b4efea7f83547bf11eb3ef5ea6f8e1
        env:
        - name: ZOOKEEPER
          value: zookeeper.kafka:2181
        - name: BOOTSTRAP
          value: "bootstrap.kafka:9092"
        # the following must be edited per job, must be a single topic or comma separated list of topics 
        - name: OUTPUT_TOPICS
          value: "test-max-rssi,test-raw-messages" 
        # the following must be edited per job
        - name: APPLICATION_ID
          value: "Enrich_Messages"
        # the following are optional, if blank will not be used
        - name: INPUT_TOPICS  # Comma separated list of topics
          value: ""
        - name: INTERMEDIATE_TOPICS  # Comma separated list of topics
          value: ""
        command:
        - /bin/bash
        - -ce
        - >
          if [ -z "$OUTPUT_TOPICS" ]; then
            echo "Please set the TOPICS env (comma-separated) and re-create the job"
            tail -f /dev/null
          fi

          if [ -z "$BOOTSTRAP" ]; then
            echo "Please set the broker BOOTSTRAP env and re-create the job"
            tail -f /dev/null
          fi

          if [ -z "$APPLICATION_ID" ]; then
            echo "Please set the APPLICATION_ID env and re-create the job"
            tail -f /dev/null
          fi

          echo "OUTPUT TOPICS TO DELETE:";
          echo -n $OUTPUT_TOPICS | sed 's/,/\n/g';

          ./bin/kafka-topics.sh --zookeeper $ZOOKEEPER --delete --topic $OUTPUT_TOPICS;

          echo "Finished deleting topics...";

          CMD_STRING="";
          if [ -z "$INPUT_TOPICS" ]; then
            echo "No INPUT_TOPICS supplied - no input topic offsets will be altered"
          else 
            CMD_STRING+="--input-topics $INPUT_TOPICS "
          fi

          if [ -z "$INTERMEDIATE_TOPICS" ]; then
            echo "No INTERMEDIATE_TOPICS supplied - no through topic offsets will be altered"
          else 
            CMD_STRING+="--intermediate-topics $INTERMEDIATE_TOPICS "
          fi

          echo "# Starting application reset!";
          ./bin/kafka-streams-application-reset.sh --bootstrap-servers "$BOOTSTRAP" --application-id "$APPLICATION_ID" "$CMD_STRING";
          echo "# Finished application reset!"
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 3
instruction: We need to deploy a Kubernetes Job named `delete-topics` in the `kafka` namespace to delete specified Kafka topics and reset the application state. The job should use the Docker image `solsson/kafka:2.1.1@sha256:8bc8242c649c395ab79d76cc83b1052e63b4efea7f83547bf11eb3ef5ea6f8e1`. It must connect to a Zookeeper instance at `zookeeper.kafka:2181` and a Kafka broker at `bootstrap.kafka:9092`. The job should delete the topics `test-max-rssi` and `test-raw-messages`, and reset the application state with the ID `Enrich_Messages`. The job should also allow for optional input and intermediate topics to be specified, which will alter the offsets of these topics if provided. The job should not restart once started and should have a backoff limit of 3 retries. Please ensure the job script checks for the required environment variables and exits gracefully if they are not set.

kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: zookeeper-config
  namespace: kafka
apiVersion: v1
data:
  init.sh: |-
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e
    set -x

    [ ! -d /var/lib/zookeeper/data ] && mkdir -m 770 /var/lib/zookeeper/data && chgrp $(stat -c '%g' /var/lib/zookeeper) /var/lib/zookeeper/data
    [ -z "$ID_OFFSET" ] && ID_OFFSET=1
    export ZOOKEEPER_SERVER_ID=$((${HOSTNAME##*-} + $ID_OFFSET))
    echo "${ZOOKEEPER_SERVER_ID:-1}" | tee /var/lib/zookeeper/data/myid
    cp -Lur /etc/kafka-configmap/* /etc/kafka/
    [ ! -z "$PZOO_REPLICAS" ] && [ ! -z "$REPLICAS" ] && {
      sed -i "s/^server\\./#server./" /etc/kafka/zookeeper.properties
      for N in $(seq $PZOO_REPLICAS); do echo "server.$N=pzoo-$(( $N - 1 )).pzoo.$POD_NAMESPACE.svc.cluster.local:2888:3888:participant" >> /etc/kafka/zookeeper.properties; done
      for N in $(seq $(( $REPLICAS - $PZOO_REPLICAS ))); do echo "server.$(( $PZOO_REPLICAS + $N ))=zoo-$(( $N - 1 )).zoo.$POD_NAMESPACE.svc.cluster.local:2888:3888:participant" >> /etc/kafka/zookeeper.properties; done
    }
    ln -s /etc/kafka/zookeeper.properties /etc/kafka/zookeeper.properties.scale-5.$POD_NAME

  zookeeper.properties: |
    authProvider.1=org.apache.zookeeper.server.auth.SASLAuthenticationProvider
    requireClientAuthScheme=sasl
    jaasLoginRenew=3600000

    4lw.commands.whitelist=ruok
    tickTime=2000
    dataDir=/var/lib/zookeeper/data
    dataLogDir=/var/lib/zookeeper/log
    clientPort=2181
    maxClientCnxns=3
    initLimit=5
    syncLimit=2
    tcpKeepAlive=true
    electionPortBindRetry=0
    server.1=pzoo-0.pzoo:2888:3888:participant
    server.2=pzoo-1.pzoo:2888:3888:participant
    server.3=pzoo-2.pzoo:2888:3888:participant
    server.4=zoo-0.zoo:2888:3888:participant
    server.5=zoo-1.zoo:2888:3888:participant

  zookeeper_jaas.conf: |
    Server {
      org.apache.zookeeper.server.auth.DigestLoginModule required
      user_super="zookeeper"
      user_admin="admin-secret";
    };

  log4j.properties: |-
    log4j.rootLogger=INFO, stdout
    log4j.appender.stdout=org.apache.log4j.ConsoleAppender
    log4j.appender.stdout.layout=org.apache.log4j.PatternLayout
    log4j.appender.stdout.layout.ConversionPattern=[%d] %p %m (%c)%n

    # Suppress connection log messages, one line per readiness probe
    log4j.logger.org.apache.zookeeper.server.NIOServerCnxn=WARN
instruction: We need to deploy a ConfigMap named `zookeeper-config` in the `kafka` namespace that includes several configuration files for a Zookeeper setup. The ConfigMap should contain an `init.sh` script to initialize Zookeeper data and set the server ID, a `zookeeper.properties` file with specific Zookeeper configurations including SASL authentication, a `zookeeper_jaas.conf` file for JAAS configuration, and a `log4j.properties` file for logging settings. The `init.sh` script should handle the creation of the Zookeeper data directory, setting the server ID based on the hostname and an optional ID offset, copying configuration files, and updating the `zookeeper.properties` file with server entries based on the number of replicas and participant Zookeeper servers. Additionally, the `zookeeper.properties` file should include settings for client authentication, connection limits, and server synchronization, while the `log4j.properties` file should suppress certain log messages for readiness probes.

          imagePullPolicy: "IfNotPresent"

            privileged: true
          env:

            - name: KAFKA_NODES

            privileged: true
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: env
            - configMapRef:
                name: configzookeeperenv
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /var/log/contrail

            - name: NODE_TYPE

            privileged: true

            - configMapRef:
                name: contrail-analyticsdb-config
            - configMapRef:
                name: nodemgr-config
          env:
            - name: NODE_TYPE
              value: analytics-alarm
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /var/log/contrail
              name: analytics-alarm-logs
            - mountPath: /mnt
              name: docker-unix-socket

        - name: contrail-analytics-alarm-provisioner
          image: "hub.juniper.net/contrail/contrail-provisioner:2011.138"
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: env
            - configMapRef:
                name: defaults-env
            - configMapRef:
                name: contrail-analyticsdb-config
            - configMapRef:
                name: nodemgr-config
          env:
            - name: NODE_TYPE
              value: analytics-alarm
          volumeMounts:

              name: analytics-alarm-logs

        - name: contrail-registry

        - name: analytics-alarm-logs

            path: /var/log/contrail/analytics-alarm
        - name: host-var-lib
          hostPath:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: kafka-consumer
  labels:
    app: kafka-consumer
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kafka-consumer
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: kafka-consumer
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: kafka-consumer
          image: quay.io/fvaleri/kafka-client:latest
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          env:
            - name: KAFKA_OPTS
              value: "-Dcom.redhat.fips=false"
            - name: CLIENT_TYPE
              value: "consumer"
            - name: BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS
              value: "my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap:9092"
            - name: SECURITY_PROTOCOL
              value: "PLAINTEXT"
            - name: TOPIC_NAME
              value: "my-topic"
            - name: NUM_MESSAGES
              value: "100"
            - name: PROC_DELAY_MS
              value: "1000"
          resources:
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 200Mi
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 100Mi
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 100
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchExpressions:
                    - key: app
                      operator: In
                      values:
                        - kafka-consumer
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
instruction: We need to deploy a Kafka consumer application using a Kubernetes Deployment. The deployment should have exactly one replica and use the image `quay.io/fvaleri/kafka-client:latest` with the `Always` pull policy. The container should run with the environment variables `KAFKA_OPTS`, `CLIENT_TYPE`, `BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS`, `SECURITY_PROTOCOL`, `TOPIC_NAME`, and `NUM_MESSAGES` set to `-Dcom.redhat.fips=false`, `consumer`, `my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap:9092`, `PLAINTEXT`, `my-topic`, and `100` respectively. Additionally, the `PROC_DELAY_MS` environment variable should be set to `1000`. The container should have resource limits of 200m CPU and 200Mi memory, and requests of 100m CPU and 100Mi memory. To ensure that no two consumer pods run on the same node, the deployment should include pod anti-affinity with a preferred scheduling rule based on the `app` label `kafka-consumer` and the topology key `kubernetes.io/hostname`.

            - name: KEY1

            - name: NEXT_SERVICE

                configMapKeyRef:

                  key: bankService
            - name: PAYPAL_SERVICE
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: paymentservice-config
                  key: paypalService
            - name: CREDITCARD_SERVICE
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: paymentservice-config
                  key: creditCardService

              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:

                  key: databaseName

              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: paymentservice-config
                  key: group_id
            - name: KAFKA
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:

  namespace: iov-dev01

  - Ingress

    - protocol: TCP

      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app.kubernetes.io/name: "ingress-nginx-vpc"
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
  # allow access from istio
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: istio-system
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 15001
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 15006
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 15020
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 15021

  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:

      podSelector:

    - protocol: TCP

  egress:

    - protocol: TCP
      #port range
      port: 15010
    - protocol: TCP
      #port range
      port: 15012
    - protocol: TCP
      #port range
      port: 15014
    - protocol: TCP
      #port range
      port: 15021
  #allow access to istio jaeger
  #allow access to tracing by skywalking
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: tracing
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: app-trace
          component: oap
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 11800
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 12800
  # allow access to mysql
  - to:
    - ipBlock:

    - protocol: TCP

  #- to:

  #      cidr: 172.17.0.0/16
  #  ports:
  #  - protocol: TCP
  #    port: 2181
  # allow access to etcd
  # allow access to consul
  # allow access to thirdparty api
  # allow access to kafka
  # allow access to rocketmq
  # allow access to pulsar
  # allow access to elasticsearch
  # allow access to clickhouse
  # allow access to nacos
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: nacos
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: nacos-cluster
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8848
  # allow access to seata
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: seata
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app.kubernetes.io/name: seata-ha-server
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port:  8091

  # allow access to xxl-job client in iov-dev01
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: iov-dev01
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9999

            - name: MESSAGE_COUNT
              value: "100"
            - name: MESSAGE
              value: Hello-world
            - name: PRODUCER_ACKS
              value: all
            - name: LOG_LEVEL
              value: DEBUG
          image: quay.io/strimzi-test-clients/test-client-kafka-producer:latest-kafka-3.0.0
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          name: kafka-producer-client
      restartPolicy: "Never"

The job should use the image `quay.io/strimzi-test-clients/test-client-kafka-producer:latest-kafka-3.0.0` with the `imagePullPolicy` set to `IfNotPresent`. It should connect to the Kafka cluster using the `BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS` environment variable set to `my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap:9092`, and produce 100 messages to the topic `my-topic` with each message being "Hello-world". apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: kafka-manager
  namespace: default
  labels:
    app: kafka-manager
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kafka-manager
#  minReadySeconds: 60     #滚动升级时60s后认为该pod就绪
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:  ##由于replicas为3,则整个升级,pod个数在2-4个之间
      maxSurge: 1      #滚动升级时会先启动1个pod
      maxUnavailable: 1 #滚动升级时允许的最大Unavailable的pod个数
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: kafka-manager
    spec:
      #nodeSelector:  #	指派特定的节点
      #  env: test-team
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60 ##k8s将会给应用发送SIGTERM信号，可以用来正确、优雅地关闭应用,默认为30秒
      #imagePullSecrets:
      #- name: registrykey-ali-ext
      containers:
      - name: kafka-manager
        image: slpcat/kafka-manager:v3.0.0.5
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        livenessProbe: #kubernetes认为该pod是存活的,不存活则需要重启
          tcpSocket:
            port: 9000
          initialDelaySeconds: 60 ## equals to the maximum startup time of the application + couple of seconds
          timeoutSeconds: 5
          successThreshold: 1
          failureThreshold: 5
        readinessProbe: #kubernetes认为该pod是启动成功的
          tcpSocket:
            port: 9000
          initialDelaySeconds: 30 ## equals to minimum startup time of the application
          timeoutSeconds: 5
          successThreshold: 1
          failureThreshold: 5
        resources:
          # keep request = limit to keep this container in guaranteed class
          requests:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 1000m
            memory: 2Gi
        securityContext:
          capabilities: {}
          privileged: false
        env:
          - name: ZK_HOSTS
            value: "zk-km-cs:2181"
          - name: KAFKA_MANAGER_AUTH_ENABLED
            value: "true"
          - name: KAFKA_MANAGER_USERNAME
            value: "admin"
          - name: KAFKA_MANAGER_PASSWORD
            value: "password"
          - name: JAVA_OPTS
            value: "-server -Djava.awt.headless=true -Djava.nio.channels.spi.SelectorProvider=sun.nio.ch.EPollSelectorProvider -Xverify:none -XX:MetaspaceSize=128m -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m -XX:ReservedCodeCacheSize=240M -XshowSettings:vm -XX:-UseBiasedLocking -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+ExplicitGCInvokesConcurrent -XX:SoftRefLRUPolicyMSPerMB=0 -XX:G1ReservePercent=25 -XX:G1NewSizePercent=10 -XX:G1MaxNewSizePercent=25 -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=20 -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow -XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled -XX:ParallelGCThreads=8 -XX:MaxTenuringThreshold=1 -XX:G1HeapWastePercent=10 -XX:SurvivorRatio=8 -XX:G1MixedGCCountTarget=16 -XX:G1MixedGCLiveThresholdPercent=90 -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=35 -XX:G1HeapRegionSize=32m -XX:+PerfDisableSharedMem -XX:-ResizePLAB"
        ports:
          - name: http
            containerPort: 9000
instruction: We need to deploy a Kafka Manager in the `default` namespace using Kubernetes. The deployment should have exactly one replica and use the `slpcat/kafka-manager:v3.0.0.5` Docker image with an `Always` pull policy. The container should be configured with specific resource requests and limits: 500m CPU and 512Mi memory for requests, and 1000m CPU and 2Gi memory for limits. Additionally, the deployment should include liveness and readiness probes that check port 9000 with initial delays of 60 and 30 seconds, respectively, and a timeout of 5 seconds. The deployment strategy should allow for a rolling update with a maximum surge of 1 and a maximum unavailable of 1. The container should also have specific environment variables set, including `ZK_HOSTS`, `KAFKA_MANAGER_AUTH_ENABLED`, `KAFKA_MANAGER_USERNAME`, `KAFKA_MANAGER_PASSWORD`, and `JAVA_OPTS` with detailed JVM options. Finally, the container should expose port 9000 as `http`.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gatewaykafka
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gatewaykafka
      version: 'v1'
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gatewaykafka
        version: 'v1'
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchExpressions:
                    - key: app
                      operator: In
                      values:
                        - gatewaykafka
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
              weight: 100
      initContainers:
        - name: init-ds
          image: busybox:latest
          command:
            - '/bin/sh'
            - '-c'
            - |
              while true
              do
                rt=$(nc -z -w 1 gatewaykafka-postgresql 5432)
                if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
                  echo "DB is UP"
                  break
                fi
                echo "DB is not yet reachable;sleep for 10s before retry"
                sleep 10
              done
      containers:
        - name: gatewaykafka-app
          image: azrulhasni/gatewaykafka
          env:
            - name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
              value: prod
            - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_URI
              value: http://admin:${jhipster.registry.password}@jhipster-registry.default.svc.cluster.local:8761/config
            - name: JHIPSTER_REGISTRY_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: registry-secret
                  key: registry-admin-password
            - name: EUREKA_CLIENT_SERVICE_URL_DEFAULTZONE
              value: http://admin:${jhipster.registry.password}@jhipster-registry.default.svc.cluster.local:8761/eureka/
            - name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL
              value: jdbc:postgresql://gatewaykafka-postgresql.default.svc.cluster.local:5432/GatewayKafka
            - name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME
              value: GatewayKafka
            - name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: gatewaykafka-postgresql
                  key: postgresql-password
            - name: SPRING_SLEUTH_PROPAGATION_KEYS
              value: 'x-request-id,x-ot-span-context'
            - name: JAVA_OPTS
              value: ' -Xmx256m -Xms256m'
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: '512Mi'
              cpu: '500m'
            limits:
              memory: '1Gi'
              cpu: '1'
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /management/health
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 15
            failureThreshold: 6
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /management/health
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 120

kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: zookeeper-config
  namespace: default
apiVersion: v1
data:
  init.sh: |-
    #!/bin/bash
    set -x

    [ -z "$ID_OFFSET" ] && ID_OFFSET=1
    export ZOOKEEPER_SERVER_ID=$((${HOSTNAME##*-} + $ID_OFFSET))
    echo "${ZOOKEEPER_SERVER_ID:-1}" | tee /var/lib/zookeeper/data/myid
    sed -i "s/server\.$ZOOKEEPER_SERVER_ID\=[a-z0-9.-]*/server.$ZOOKEEPER_SERVER_ID=0.0.0.0/" /etc/kafka/zookeeper.properties

  zookeeper.properties: |-
    tickTime=2000
    dataDir=/var/lib/zookeeper/data
    dataLogDir=/var/lib/zookeeper/log
    clientPort=2181
    initLimit=5
    syncLimit=2
    server.1=zoo-0.zoo:2888:3888:participant
    server.2=zoo-1.zoo:2888:3888:participant
    server.3=zoo-2.zoo:2888:3888:participant

  log4j.properties: |-
    log4j.rootLogger=INFO, stdout
    log4j.appender.stdout=org.apache.log4j.ConsoleAppender
    log4j.appender.stdout.layout=org.apache.log4j.PatternLayout
    log4j.appender.stdout.layout.ConversionPattern=[%d] %p %m (%c)%n

    # Suppress connection log messages, three lines per livenessProbe execution
    log4j.logger.org.apache.zookeeper.server.NIOServerCnxnFactory=WARN
    log4j.logger.org.apache.zookeeper.server.NIOServerCnxn=WARN
instruction: We need to deploy a ConfigMap named `zookeeper-config` in the `default` namespace to configure a ZooKeeper cluster. The ConfigMap should include an `init.sh` script that sets up the ZooKeeper server ID and updates the `zookeeper.properties` file accordingly. Additionally, the ConfigMap should contain the `zookeeper.properties` file with specific configurations such as `tickTime`, `dataDir`, `dataLogDir`, `clientPort`, `initLimit`, `syncLimit`, and server definitions for three ZooKeeper nodes. Lastly, include a `log4j.properties` file to configure logging levels and suppress unnecessary connection log messages.

    {%- if features.async.kafka.install and 'url' not in features.async.kafka %}
    
    features.feature.async-api.endpoint-KAFKA={{name}}-kafka-kafka-bootstrap.<apps-subdomain>:443
    {%- elif features.async.kafka.install and 'url' in features.async.kafka %}

    {% endif %}

    # Application configuration properties

    mocks.rest.enable-cors-policy=${ENABLE_CORS_POLICY:true}

    # Keycloak configuration properties

    keycloak.realm={{keycloak.realm}}
    keycloak.resource=microcks-app
    keycloak.use-resource-role-mappings=true
    keycloak.bearer-only=true

content:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: consume-container-itgtests-job
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      name: consume-container-itgtests-job
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: itgtests
      containers:
      - name: ibmcase-python
        image: docker-registry.default.svc:5000/itgtests/ibmcase-python:test
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        command: ["bash", "-c" ]
        args:
          - >
              echo "This is the job for consuming containers from the containers Kafka topic" &&
              mkdir ${WORKING_DIR} && cd ${WORKING_DIR} &&
              git clone ${GITHUB_REPO} && cd ${REPO_NAME} && if [ "master" != "${BRANCH}" ]; then git checkout ${BRANCH}; fi &&
              cd ${ITGTESTS_LOCATION} &&
              export PYTHONPATH=${PYTHONPATH}:${WORKING_DIR}/${REPO_NAME}/itg-tests && 
              python -u ConsumeContainers.py ${CONTAINER_ID} ${TOPIC_NAME}
              # The -u flag above is for python to run in unbuffered mode: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51362213/docker-compose-not-printing-stdout-in-python-app
        env:
        # Your working directory within the container
        - name: WORKING_DIR
          value: "/tmp/github"
        # Github repository containing the integration tests to be executed
        - name: GITHUB_REPO
          value: "https://github.com/ldesrosi/refarch-kc.git"
        # Specific branch for the integration tests
        - name: BRANCH
          value: "master"
        # Name of the repository
        - name: REPO_NAME
          value: "refarch-kc"
        # Location of the integration tests folder within the repository
        - name: ITGTESTS_LOCATION
          value: "itg-tests/ContainersPython"
        # Container ID to be send
        - name: CONTAINER_ID
          value: "regOCP_01"
        # Event Streams topic name which the event will be sent to
        - name: TOPIC_NAME
          value: "itgtest"
        # Event Streams Kafka brokers. You MUST create a configmap in advance with the brokers information:
        # oc create configmap kafka-brokers --from-literal=brokers='<replace with comma-separated list of brokers>' -n <namespace>
        # You can find the list of brokers either in the Event Streams UI or when you login through the CLI: cloudctl es init
        - name: KAFKA_BROKERS
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: "kafka-brokers"
              key: brokers
        # Based on this parameter we add the appropriate certificates for when Event Streams is hosted either on ICP or OCP
        - name: KAFKA_ENV
          value: "OCP"
        # Location of your Event Streams pem certificate for ssl connections. You MUST download it in advance.
        # This can be downloaded from the Event Streams UI.
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 0
instruction: We need to deploy a Kubernetes Job named `consume-container-itgtests-job` that runs a container from the image `docker-registry.default.svc:5000/itgtests/ibmcase-python:test` with the `Always` pull policy. The container should execute a series of bash commands to clone a GitHub repository, check out a specific branch, and run a Python script `ConsumeContainers.py` with specified parameters. The job must use the `itgtests` service account and should not be restarted (`restartPolicy: Never`). Additionally, the job should have no backoff limit (`backoffLimit: 0`). The environment variables `WORKING_DIR`, `GITHUB_REPO`, `BRANCH`, `REPO_NAME`, `ITGTESTS_LOCATION`, `CONTAINER_ID`, `TOPIC_NAME`, `KAFKA_BROKERS`, `KAFKA_ENV`, and the location of the Event Streams pem certificate must be set as specified in the manifest.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: strimzi-cluster-operator
  labels:
    app: strimzi
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      name: strimzi-cluster-operator
      strimzi.io/kind: cluster-operator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        name: strimzi-cluster-operator
        strimzi.io/kind: cluster-operator
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: strimzi-cluster-operator
      volumes:
        - name: strimzi-tmp
          emptyDir:
            medium: Memory
            sizeLimit: 1Mi
        - name: co-config-volume
          configMap:
            name: strimzi-cluster-operator
      containers:
        - name: strimzi-cluster-operator
          image: quay.io/strimzi/operator:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
          args:
            - /opt/strimzi/bin/cluster_operator_run.sh
          volumeMounts:
            - name: strimzi-tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
            - name: co-config-volume
              mountPath: /opt/strimzi/custom-config/
          env:
            - name: STRIMZI_NAMESPACE
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.namespace
            - name: STRIMZI_FULL_RECONCILIATION_INTERVAL_MS
              value: "120000"
            - name: STRIMZI_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS
              value: "300000"
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_TLS_SIDECAR_ENTITY_OPERATOR_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.2.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_EXPORTER_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.2.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_CRUISE_CONTROL_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.2.0
            - name: STRIMZI_KAFKA_IMAGES
              value: |
                3.1.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.0
                3.1.1=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.1
                3.2.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.2.0
            - name: STRIMZI_KAFKA_CONNECT_IMAGES
              value: |
                3.1.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.0
                3.1.1=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.1
                3.2.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.2.0
            - name: STRIMZI_KAFKA_MIRROR_MAKER_IMAGES
              value: |
                3.1.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.0
                3.1.1=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.1
                3.2.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.2.0
            - name: STRIMZI_KAFKA_MIRROR_MAKER_2_IMAGES
              value: |
                3.1.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.0
                3.1.1=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.1.1
                3.2.0=quay.io/strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-3.2.0
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_TOPIC_OPERATOR_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/operator:latest
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_USER_OPERATOR_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/operator:latest
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_INIT_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/operator:latest
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_BRIDGE_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/kafka-bridge:0.21.5
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_JMXTRANS_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/jmxtrans:latest
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KANIKO_EXECUTOR_IMAGE
              value: quay.io/strimzi/kaniko-executor:latest
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_MAVEN_BUILDER
              value: quay.io/strimzi/maven-builder:latest
            - name: STRIMZI_OPERATOR_NAMESPACE
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.namespace
            - name: STRIMZI_FEATURE_GATES
              value: ""
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthy
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 30
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 30
          resources:
            limits:
              cpu: 1000m
              memory: 384Mi
            requests:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 384Mi
  strategy:
    type: Recreate

It should run with the `strimzi-cluster-operator` service account and include two volumes: an emptyDir volume named `strimzi-tmp` with a size limit of 1Mi in memory, and a configMap volume named `co-config-volume` sourced from the `strimzi-cluster-operator` configMap. The container should mount these volumes at `/tmp` and `/opt/strimzi/custom-config/`, respectively. Additionally, it should expose port 8080 for HTTP communication, set specific environment variables for reconciliation intervals, operation timeouts, and default images for various Kafka components, and configure liveness and readiness probes with an initial delay of 10 seconds and a period of 30 seconds. kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: collector-config
apiVersion: v1
data:
  production.conf: |-
      collector {
        # The collector runs as a web service specified on the following interface and port.
        interface = "0.0.0.0"
        port = 8080

        # The collector responds with a cookie to requests with a path that matches the 'vendor/version' protocol.
        # The expected values are:
        # - com.snowplowanalytics.snowplow/tp2 for Tracker Protocol 2
        # - r/tp2 for redirects
        # - com.snowplowanalytics.iglu/v1 for the Iglu Webhook
        # Any path that matches the 'vendor/version' protocol will result in a cookie response, for use by custom webhooks
        # downstream of the collector.
        # But you can also map any valid (i.e. two-segment) path to one of the three defaults.
        # Your custom path must be the key and the value must be one of the corresponding default paths. Both must be full
        # valid paths starting with a leading slash.
        # Pass in an empty map to avoid mapping.
        paths {
          # "/com.acme/track" = "/com.snowplowanalytics.snowplow/tp2"
          # "/com.acme/redirect" = "/r/tp2"
          # "/com.acme/iglu" = "/com.snowplowanalytics.iglu/v1"
        }

        # Configure the P3P policy header.
        p3p {
          policyRef = "/w3c/p3p.xml"
          CP = "NOI DSP COR NID PSA OUR IND COM NAV STA"
        }
        # Cross domain policy configuration.
        # If "enabled" is set to "false", the collector will respond with a 404 to the /crossdomain.xml
        # route.
        crossDomain {
          enabled = false
          # Domains that are granted access, *.acme.com will match http://acme.com and http://sub.acme.com
          domains = [ "*" ]
          # Whether to only grant access to HTTPS or both HTTPS and HTTP sources
          secure = true
        }
        # The collector returns a cookie to clients for user identification
        # with the following domain and expiration.
        cookie {
          enabled = true
          expiration = "365 days"
          # Network cookie name
          name = snowplow
          # The domain is optional and will make the cookie accessible to other
          # applications on the domain. Comment out this line to tie cookies to
          # the collector's full domain
          # domain = "{{cookieDomain}}"
          secure = false
          httpOnly = false
        }
        # If you have a do not track cookie in place, the Scala Stream Collector can respect it by
        # completely bypassing the processing of an incoming request carrying this cookie, the collector
        # will simply reply by a 200 saying "do not track".
        # The cookie name and value must match the configuration below.
        doNotTrackCookie {
          enabled = false
          name = snowplow_do_not_track
          value = snowplow_do_not_track_value
        }
        # When enabled and the cookie specified above is missing, performs a redirect to itself to check
        # if third-party cookies are blocked using the specified name. If they are indeed blocked,
        # fallbackNetworkId is used instead of generating a new random one.
        cookieBounce {
          enabled = false
          # The name of the request parameter which will be used on redirects checking that third-party
          # cookies work.
          name = "n3pc"
          # Network user id to fallback to when third-party cookies are blocked.
          fallbackNetworkUserId = "00000000-0000-4000-A000-000000000000"
          # Optionally, specify the name of the header containing the originating protocol for use in the
          # bounce redirect location. Use this if behind a load balancer that performs SSL termination.
          # The value of this header must be http or https. Example, if behind an AWS Classic ELB.
          forwardedProtocolHeader = "X-Forwarded-Proto"
        }
        # When enabled, the redirect url passed via the `u` query parameter is scanned for a placeholder
        # token. All instances of that token are replaced withe the network ID. If the placeholder isn't
        # specified, the default value is `${SP_NUID}`.
        redirectMacro {
          enabled = false
          # Optional custom placeholder token (defaults to the literal `${SP_NUID}`)
          # placeholder = "[TOKEN]"
        }
        # Customize response handling for requests for the root path ("/").
        # Useful if you need to redirect to web content or privacy policies regarding the use of this collector.
        rootResponse {
          enabled = false
          statusCode = 302
          # Optional, defaults to empty map
          headers = {
              Location = "https://127.0.0.1/",
              X-Custom = "something"
          }
          # Optional, defaults to empty string
          body = "302, redirecting"
        }

        # Configuration related to CORS preflight requests
        cors {
          # The Access-Control-Max-Age response header indicates how long the results of a preflight
          # request can be cached. -1 seconds disables the cache. Chromium max is 10m, Firefox is 24h.
          accessControlMaxAge = 5 seconds
        }

        # Configuration of prometheus http metrics
        prometheusMetrics {
          # If metrics are enabled then all requests will be logged as prometheus metrics
          # and '/metrics' endpoint will return the report about the requests
          enabled = false
          # Custom buckets for http_request_duration_seconds_bucket duration metric
          #durationBucketsInSeconds = [0.1, 3, 10]
        }

        streams {
          # Events which have successfully been collected will be stored in the good stream/topic
          good = good
          # Events that are too big (w.r.t Kinesis 1MB limit) will be stored in the bad stream/topic
          bad = bad
          # Whether to use the incoming event's ip as the partition key for the good stream/topic
          # Note: Nsq does not make use of partition key.
          useIpAddressAsPartitionKey = false
          # Enable the chosen sink by uncommenting the appropriate configuration
          sink {
            # Choose between kinesis, google-pub-sub, kafka, nsq, or stdout.
            # To use stdout, comment or remove everything in the "collector.streams.sink" section except
            # "enabled" which should be set to "stdout".
            enabled =

            # Or Google Pubsub
            googleProjectId = your-project
            ## Minimum, maximum and total backoff periods, in milliseconds
            ## and multiplier between two backoff
            backoffPolicy {
              minBackoff = 100
              maxBackoff = 1000
              totalBackoff = 10000
              multiplier = 1.1
            }
          }
          # Incoming events are stored in a buffer before being sent to Kinesis/Kafka.
          # Note: Buffering is not supported by NSQ.
          # The buffer is emptied whenever:
          # - the number of stored records reaches record-limit or
          # - the combined size of the stored records reaches byte-limit or
          # - the time in milliseconds since the buffer was last emptied reaches time-limit
          buffer {
            byteLimit = 1000000
            recordLimit = 10
            timeLimit = 1000
          }
        }
      }
      # Akka has a variety of possible configuration options defined at
      # http://doc.akka.io/docs/akka/current/scala/general/configuration.html
      akka {
        loglevel = DEBUG # 'OFF' for no logging, 'DEBUG' for all logging.
        loggers = ["akka.event.slf4j.Slf4jLogger"]
        # akka-http is the server the Stream collector uses and has configurable options defined at
        # http://doc.akka.io/docs/akka-http/current/scala/http/configuration.html
        http.server {
          # To obtain the hostname in the collector, the 'remote-address' header
          # should be set. By default, this is disabled, and enabling it
          # adds the 'Remote-Address' header to every request automatically.
          remote-address-header = on
          raw-request-uri-header = on
          # Define the maximum request length (the default is 2048)
          parsing {
            max-uri-length = 32768
            uri-parsing-mode = relaxed
          }
        }
      }
instruction: We need to deploy a ConfigMap named `collector-config` that contains the configuration for the Snowplow collector service. The ConfigMap should include settings for the collector's web service interface and port (0.0.0.0:8080), P3P policy header, cross-domain policy, cookie configuration, and CORS preflight requests. Additionally, it should specify the paths for different protocols (e.g., Tracker Protocol 2, redirects, Iglu Webhook), enable or disable certain features like Prometheus metrics, and configure the streams for good and bad events. The buffer settings for incoming events should be set to a byte limit of 1,000,000, a record limit of 10, and a time limit of 1,000 milliseconds. The Akka logging level should be set to DEBUG, and the HTTP server should have the remote-address-header and raw-request-uri-header enabled with a maximum URI length of 32,768.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    service: subscription-manager
  name: subscription-manager
  namespace: scorpio-broker
spec:
  progressDeadlineSeconds: 600
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 10
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      service: subscription-manager
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        service: subscription-manager
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: ibn40/digitaltwin:SubscriptionManager_test
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: subscription-manager
        env:                            #edited
        - name: KAFKA_BROKERS
          value: "my-cluster-kafka-brokers"
        - name: KAFKA_PORT
          value: "9092"
        - name: KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP
          value: "my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 2025
          protocol: TCP
        lifecycle:
           preStop:
            exec:
              command:
              - /bin/sh
              - -c
              - curl -X PUT "http://eureka:8761/eureka/apps/SUBSCRIPTION-MANAGER/$HOSTNAME:subscription-manager:2025/status?value=OUT_OF_SERVICE"
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - curl --silent http://localhost:2025/actuator/health | grep --quiet -e
              '^{\"status\"\:\"UP\".*}$'
          failureThreshold: 10
          initialDelaySeconds: 20
          periodSeconds: 5
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 1280Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 600Mi
      restartPolicy: Always
      serviceAccountName: ""
status: {}
instruction: We need to deploy a Kubernetes Deployment named `subscription-manager` in the `scorpio-broker` namespace. The deployment should use the Docker image `ibn40/digitaltwin:SubscriptionManager_test` with the `imagePullPolicy` set to `Always`. It should run a single replica and maintain a revision history limit of 10. The rolling update strategy should allow up to 25% max surge and max unavailable instances. The container should expose port 2025, have environment variables `KAFKA_BROKERS`, `KAFKA_PORT`, and `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP` set to `my-cluster-kafka-brokers`, `9092`, and `my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap` respectively. Additionally, it should have resource limits of 500m CPU and 1280Mi memory, with requests of 250m CPU and 600Mi memory. The readiness probe should check the health endpoint every 5 seconds starting 20 seconds after the container starts, with a failure threshold of 10. The preStop hook should update the Eureka service status to `OUT_OF_SERVICE`.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: kafka-source-dispatcher
  namespace: knative-eventing
  labels:
    app: kafka-source-dispatcher
    kafka.eventing.knative.dev/release: devel
spec:
  serviceName: kafka-source-dispatcher
  podManagementPolicy: "Parallel"
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kafka-source-dispatcher
  template:
    metadata:
      name: kafka-source-dispatcher
      labels:
        app: kafka-source-dispatcher
        app.kubernetes.io/component: kafka-dispatcher
        kafka.eventing.knative.dev/release: devel
    spec:
      # To avoid node becoming SPOF, spread our replicas to different nodes and zones.
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 2
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: kafka-source-dispatcher
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchLabels:
                    app: kafka-source-dispatcher
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
              weight: 100
      serviceAccountName: knative-kafka-source-data-plane
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: kafka-source-dispatcher
          image: ${KNATIVE_KAFKA_DISPATCHER_IMAGE}
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /etc/config
              name: config-kafka-source-data-plane
              readOnly: true
            - mountPath: /etc/contract-resources
              name: contract-resources
              readOnly: true
            - mountPath: /tmp
              name: cache
            - mountPath: /etc/logging
              name: kafka-config-logging
              readOnly: true
            - mountPath: /etc/tracing
              name: config-tracing
              readOnly: true
          ports:
            - containerPort: 9090
              name: http-metrics
              protocol: TCP
          env:
            - name: SERVICE_NAME
              value: "kafka-source-dispatcher"
            - name: SERVICE_NAMESPACE
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.namespace
            - name: PRODUCER_CONFIG_FILE_PATH
              value: /etc/config/config-kafka-source-producer.properties
            - name: CONSUMER_CONFIG_FILE_PATH
              value: /etc/config/config-kafka-source-consumer.properties
            - name: WEBCLIENT_CONFIG_FILE_PATH
              value: /etc/config/config-kafka-source-webclient.properties
            - name: DATA_PLANE_CONFIG_FILE_PATH
              value: /etc/contract-resources/data
            - name: EGRESSES_INITIAL_CAPACITY
              value: "20"
            - name: INSTANCE_ID
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.uid
            - name: METRICS_PATH
              value: /metrics
            - name: METRICS_PORT
              value: "9090"
            - name: METRICS_PUBLISH_QUANTILES
              value: "false"
            - name: METRICS_JVM_ENABLED
              value: "false"
            - name: CONFIG_TRACING_PATH
              value: "/etc/tracing"
            # https://github.com/fabric8io/kubernetes-client/issues/2212
            - name: HTTP2_DISABLE
              value: "true"
            # This should be set according to initial delay seconds
            - name: WAIT_STARTUP_SECONDS
              value: "8"
            - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
              value: "-XX:+CrashOnOutOfMemoryError"

          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 1000m
              # 600Mi for virtual replicas + 100Mi overhead
              memory: 700Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 2000m
              memory: 1000Mi

          livenessProbe:
            failureThreshold: 3
            tcpSocket:
              port: 9090
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 3
            successThreshold: 1
            timeoutSeconds: 1
          readinessProbe:
            failureThreshold: 3
            tcpSocket:
              port: 9090
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 3
            successThreshold: 1
            timeoutSeconds: 1
          terminationMessagePolicy: FallbackToLogsOnError
          terminationMessagePath: /dev/temination-log
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            privileged: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      volumes:
        - name: config-kafka-source-data-plane
          configMap:
            name: config-kafka-source-data-plane
        - name: cache
          emptyDir: { }
        - name: kafka-config-logging
          configMap:
            name: kafka-config-logging
        - name: config-tracing
          configMap:
            name: config-tracing
      restartPolicy: Always
      dnsConfig:
        options:
          - name: single-request-reopen
instruction: We need to deploy a StatefulSet named `kafka-source-dispatcher` in the `knative-eventing` namespace to manage Kafka source dispatchers. The StatefulSet should use the image `${KNATIVE_KAFKA_DISPATCHER_IMAGE}` with the `IfNotPresent` pull policy. Each pod should have 1000m CPU and 700Mi memory requested, and 2000m CPU and 1000Mi memory as limits. The deployment should ensure that replicas are spread across different nodes and availability zones to avoid a single point of failure. Additionally, the StatefulSet should include liveness and readiness probes on port 9090, and the container should run with restricted privileges, disallowing privilege escalation and running with a non-root user. The pod should also mount several ConfigMaps and an emptyDir volume for caching. Please ensure the deployment includes the specified environment variables, including paths to configuration files and initial capacity settings for egresses.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: spring-boot-devoxx-spring-kafka-application-yaml
type: Opaque
stringData:
  application.yaml: |
    spring:
      kafka:
        properties:      
          bootstrap.servers: kafka.europe-central2.gcp.confluent.cloud:9092
          sasl.mechanism: PLAIN
          sasl.jaas.config: "org.apache.kafka.common.security.plain.PlainLoginModule   required username='blah'   password='blah';"
          security.protocol: SASL_SSL
          streams:
            replication-factor: 3
      cloud:
        stream:
          function:
            definition: produceChuckNorris;consumeChuckNorris;processWords
            bindings:
              # input and output of KStreams topology
              processWords-in-0: facts
              processWords-out-0: counts
          bindings:
            # kafka producer
            produceChuckNorris-out-0:
              binder: kafka
              destination: facts
              producer:
                partition-count: 4
                useNativeEncoding: true
            # kafka consumer
            consumeChuckNorris-in-0:
              binder: kafka
              destination: facts
              group: myGroup
          kafka:
            binder:
              consumer-properties:
                key.deserializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer
                value.deserializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer
              producer-properties:
                key.serializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer
                value.serializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer
            streams:
              binder:
                applicationId: chuck-norris-word-count
                configuration:
                  default.key.serde: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serdes$StringSerde
                  default.value.serde: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serdes$BytesSerde
                  commit.interval.ms: 1000

Additionally, it should specify the replication factor for Kafka Streams as 3. The application should define three functions: `produceChuckNorris`, `consumeChuckNorris`, and `processWords`, with appropriate bindings for input and output destinations. The producer should have a partition count of 4 and use native encoding. The consumer should be part of the `myGroup` consumer group. Both the producer and consumer should use string serializers and deserializers. The Kafka Streams binder should have an application ID of `chuck-norris-word-count` and a commit interval of 1000 milliseconds.

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: hawkular-openshift-agent-kafkanetes
  labels:
    name: hawkular-openshift-agent-kafkanetes
    hawkular-openshift-agent-example: jolokia-wildfly
data:
  hawkular-openshift-agent: |
    endpoints:
    - type: jolokia
      protocol: http
      port: 8778
      path: /jolokia/
      collection_interval: 15s
      metrics:
      - name: kafka.server:type=ReplicaManager,name=UnderReplicatedPartitions#Value
        type: gauge
        description: "Number of under-replicated partitions"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: UnderReplicatedPartitions
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: kafka.server:type=BrokerTopicMetrics,name=MessagesInPerSec#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "Aggregate incoming message rate"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: MessagesInPerSec
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: kafka.server:type=BrokerTopicMetrics,name=BytesInPerSec#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "incoming bytes per second"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: BytesInPerSec
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: kafka.server:type=BrokerTopicMetrics,name=BytesOutPerSec#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "outgoing bytes per second"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: BytesOutPerSec
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: kafka.network:type=RequestMetrics,name=RequestsPerSec,request=Produce#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "Number of requests per second"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: RequestsPerSec/Produce
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
          metric_name: RequestsPerSec_Produce
      - name: kafka.network:type=RequestMetrics,name=RequestsPerSec,request=FetchConsumer#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "Number of requests per second"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: RequestsPerSec/FetchConsumer
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: kafka.network:type=RequestMetrics,name=RequestsPerSec,request=FetchFollower#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "Number of requests per second"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: RequestsPerSec/FetchFollower
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: afka.network:type=RequestMetrics,name=TotalTimeMs,request=Produce#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "Total time it takes to process a request. You can also monitor split times for QueueTimeMs, LocalTimeMs, RemoteTimeMs and RemoteTimeMs"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: TotalTimeMs/Produce
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: afka.network:type=RequestMetrics,name=TotalTimeMs,request=FetchConsumer#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "Total time it takes to process a request. You can also monitor split times for QueueTimeMs, LocalTimeMs, RemoteTimeMs and RemoteTimeMs"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: TotalTimeMs/FetchConsumer
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: afka.network:type=RequestMetrics,name=TotalTimeMs,request=FetchFollower#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: "Total time it takes to process a request. You can also monitor split times for QueueTimeMs, LocalTimeMs, RemoteTimeMs and RemoteTimeMs"
        tags:
          descriptor_name: TotalTimeMs/FetchFollower
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
      - name: kafka.log:type=LogFlushStats,name=LogFlushRateAndTimeMs#MeanRate
        type: gauge
        description: Asynchronous disk log flush and time in ms
        tags:
          descriptor_name: LogFlushRateAndTimeMs
          container_name: ${POD:label[deploymentconfig]}
instruction: We need to deploy a ConfigMap named `hawkular-openshift-agent-kafkanetes` that will configure the Hawkular OpenShift Agent to collect metrics from Jolokia endpoints. The ConfigMap should include specific metrics related to Kafka broker performance, such as under-replicated partitions, message rates, bytes in/out per second, request rates, and total request processing times. Each metric should be collected at an interval of 15 seconds and tagged with the deployment configuration label of the pod. Please ensure the Jolokia endpoint is accessed via HTTP on port 8778 and the path `/jolokia/`.

            initialDelaySeconds: 3

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: maxwell-bootstrap-id01
  namespace: default
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      name: maxwell-bootstrap
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: maxwell-bootstrap
        image: zendesk/maxwell
        env:
          - name: LOG_LEVEL
            value: "info"
          - name: HOST
            value: "mysql-server.dbaas"
          - name: PORT
            value: "3306"
          - name: USER
            value: "root"
          - name: PASSWORD
            value: "root_password"
          #- name: DATABASE
          #  value: "mydb"
          #- name: TABLE
          #  value: "table01"
          #- name: WHERE_CLAUSE
          #  value: "where"
          #- name: PRODUCER
          #  value: "stdout"
          - name: PRODUCER
            value: "kafka"
          - name: CLIENT_ID
            value: "maxwell"
          - name: KAFKA_BROKERS
            value: "kafka-svc:9092"
          - name: KAFKA_TOPIC
            value: "maxwell-topic"
        command: [ "/bin/sh", "-c", "bin/maxwell-bootstrap --log_level $LOG_LEVEL \
                                    --producer=$PRODUCER --host $HOST --user $USER \
                                    --password $PASSWORD --port $PORT \
                                    #--database $DATABASE --table $TABLE \
                                    --kafka.bootstrap.servers=${KAFKA_BROKERS} \
                                    --kafka_topic=$KAFKA_TOPIC \
                                    --kafka_partition_hash=murmur3 \
                                    --kafka_key_format=hash \
                                    --kafka.compression.type=snappy \
                                    --kafka.retries=5 \
                                    --kafka.acks=all \
                                    --producer_partition_by=primary_key \
                                    --bootstrapper=async " ]
      restartPolicy: Never

Additionally, the command should include specific Maxwell bootstrap parameters such as `--kafka.bootstrap.servers`, `--kafka_topic`, `--kafka_partition_hash`, `--kafka_key_format`, `--kafka.compression.type`, `--kafka.retries`, `--kafka.acks`, and `--producer_partition_by`.             - name: STRIMZI_KAFKA_CONNECT_S2I_IMAGES

                2.6.0=strimzi/kafka:latest-kafka-2.6.0
            - name: STRIMZI_KAFKA_MIRROR_MAKER_IMAGES

            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_TOPIC_OPERATOR_IMAGE

              value: strimzi/operator:latest
            - name: STRIMZI_DEFAULT_KAFKA_INIT_IMAGE

    type: Recreate

metadata:

spec:
  serviceName: taskmanager-hl
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flink
      component: taskmanager
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flink
        component: taskmanager
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 9999
        fsGroup: 9999
      containers:
      - name: taskmanager
        image: flink:1.15
        env:
          - name: ENABLE_BUILT_IN_PLUGINS
            value: "flink-s3-fs-hadoop-1.15-SNAPSHOT.jar"
          - name: POD_NAME
            valueFrom:
              fieldRef:
                fieldPath: metadata.name
        args: ["taskmanager", "-Dtaskmanager.resource-id=$(POD_NAME)"]
        ports:
        - containerPort: 6122
          name: rpc
        - containerPort: 6125
          name: query-state
        - containerPort: 6121
          name: metrics
        livenessProbe:
          tcpSocket:
            port: 6122
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 60
        volumeMounts:
        - name: flink-config-volume
          mountPath: /opt/flink/conf/
        # - name: ha-storage
        #   mountPath: /ha-storage
        - name: pv
          mountPath: /pv
      serviceAccountName: flink-service-account # Service account which has the permissions to create, edit, delete ConfigMaps
      volumes:
      - name: flink-config-volume
        configMap:
          name: flink-config
          items:
          - key: flink-conf.yaml
            path: flink-conf.yaml
          - key: log4j-console.properties
            path: log4j-console.properties
      # - name: ha-storage
      #   hostPath:
      #     path: /home/docker/flink
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: pv
    spec:
      accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
      resources:

          storage: 1Gi

- Each container must run as user `9999` with group `9999` for security context.
- The TaskManagers should expose ports 6122 (RPC), 6125 (query-state), and 6121 (metrics).
- The `ENABLE_BUILT_IN_PLUGINS` environment variable should be set to `flink-s3-fs-hadoop-1.15-SNAPSHOT.jar`, and the `POD_NAME` should be dynamically set.
- A liveness probe should be configured to check the RPC port (6122) with an initial delay of 30 seconds and a period of 60 seconds.
- Each container should mount a ConfigMap volume named `flink-config-volume` at `/opt/flink/conf/` and a PersistentVolumeClaim named `pv` at `/pv`.
- The PersistentVolumeClaim should request 1Gi of storage with `ReadWriteOnce` access mode.
- The StatefulSet should use the `flink-service-account` for permissions to manage ConfigMaps.

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cert-reflector
  namespace: cert-manager
spec:
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cert-reflector
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cert-reflector
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: cert-reflector
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/arch: amd64
      containers:
      - name: ns-watch
        image: boxboat/kubectl:1.22.1
        command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          while true; do
            echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') starting watch loop"
            kubectl get ns -w --field-selector=status.phase==Active --no-headers -o custom-columns=:metadata.name | \
            while read NS; do
              if echo "$EXCLUDED_NS" | grep -vw "$NS" > /dev/null; then
                echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') namespace - $NS"
                kubectl -n cert-manager get secret nathanpawelek-com-tls -o json | \
                  jq 'del(.metadata.namespace, .metadata.managedFields, .metadata.uid, .metadata.selfLink, .metadata.resourceVersion, .metadata.creationTimestamp)' | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f -
              fi
            done
          done
        env:
        - name: EXCLUDED_NS
          value: "cert-manager kube-system kube-node-lease kube-public default rclone metallb-system intel-gpu flux-system"
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 128Mi
            cpu: 128m
      - name: secret-watch
        image: boxboat/kubectl:1.22.1
        command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          sleep 10
          while true; do
            echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') starting watch loop"
            kubectl -n cert-manager get secret nathanpawelek-com-tls -w --no-headers -o custom-columns=:metadata.name | \
            while read SECRET; do
              EXPORT=$(kubectl -n cert-manager get secret $SECRET -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.namespace, .metadata.managedFields, .metadata.uid, .metadata.selfLink, .metadata.resourceVersion, .metadata.creationTimestamp)')
              for NS in $(kubectl get ns --field-selector=status.phase==Active --no-headers -o custom-columns=:metadata.name); do
                if echo "$EXCLUDED_NS" | grep -vw "$NS" > /dev/null; then
                  echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') namespace - $NS"
                  echo "$EXPORT" | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f -
                fi
              done
            done
          done
        env:
        - name: EXCLUDED_NS
          value: "cert-manager kube-system kube-node-lease kube-public default rclone metallb-system intel-gpu flux-system"
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 128Mi
            cpu: 128m

data:
  config: |
    last_update_time: 1649210242
    env: test
    debug: false
    # sentry_dsn: ...
    
    default_kafka_config: # https://github.com/edenhill/librdkafka/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md
      producer:
        "enable.idempotence": "true"
        "delivery.timeout.ms": "2600" # 2.6 seconds, default is "300000"
        "acks": "all"
        # "max.in.flight.requests.per.connection":  default is "1000000", after idempotence is "5"
        # "retries": default is "2147483647", after idempotence is INT32_MAX
        # "queue.buffering.max.messages": 100000
      consumer:
        "bootstrap.servers": "maggie-kafka-1:9094,maggie-kafka-2:9094,maggie-kafka-3:9094"
        "enable.auto.commit": "false"
        "auto.offset.reset": "latest"
        "max.poll.interval.ms": "50"
        # "allow.auto.create.topics": "true" -- doesn't work
    
    producers:
      p1:
        kafka_config:
          "bootstrap.servers": "maggie-kafka-1:9094,maggie-kafka-2:9094,maggie-kafka-3:9094"
      p2:
        kafka_config:
          "bootstrap.servers": "maggie-kafka-1:9094,maggie-kafka-2:9094,maggie-kafka-3:9094"
    
    http_app:
      use_producers:
        producer_ids: [p1]
      max_response_time: 6
    
    consumers:
      c1:
        kafka_topics: [ "^event-v3-.*" ]
        kafka_config:
          "group.id": "event-v3-test-group1"
          "max.poll.interval.ms": "300100"
        exclude_events: [ ^stress_test\..* ]
        use_producers:
          producer_ids: [ p1 ]
        sink:

        kafka_config:
          "group.id": "event-v3-test-group2"
          "max.poll.interval.ms": "300082"
        include_events: []
        concurrent_per_partition: 1
        use_producers:
          producer_ids: [ p2 ]
        sink:
          url: http://localhost:8081/receive_events
          method: POST
          timeout: 10
          backoff_retry_max_time: 3
    
    topic_mapping:
      - topic: event-v3-stress-test
        patterns:
          - stress_test\..*
      - topic: event-v3-test-topic5
        patterns:
          - test\.event1
      - topic: event-v3-default
        patterns:
          - .*
